what_its_for: Cefazolin is an antibiotic used to treat or prevent bacterial infections. It is commonly used for skin infections, bone and joint infections, heart infections, respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections, and to prevent infections before and after surgery. It only works against bacterial infections and will NOT treat viral infections like colds or the flu.
how_to_take: Cefazolin is given as an injection into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM) by a healthcare provider, nurse, or trained caregiver. You will not take this medication by mouth as a pill or liquid. If you are receiving this at home, your healthcare team will teach you exactly how to prepare and give the injection safely. Always wash your hands thoroughly before handling the medication or injection supplies. Use each needle and syringe only once and throw them away safely in a sharps container.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your type of infection, your weight, your kidney function, and other health conditions. Doses are typically given every 6 to 8 hours, but your schedule may be different. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor or pharmacist gave you. Do not skip doses and try to take each dose at the same time each day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store unmixed cefazolin powder at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Once mixed (reconstituted), the solution can be kept at room temperature for up to 24 hours or in the refrigerator for up to 10 days, depending on the concentration. Always check the specific storage instructions on your medication label or from your pharmacist. Do not freeze the mixed solution unless directed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use if the solution looks cloudy, discolored, or has particles in it.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting cefazolin. Avoid using blood-thinning medicines like warfarin without close monitoring, as cefazolin may increase your bleeding risk. Do not drink alcohol excessively during treatment. Do not stop taking the full course of your antibiotic early, even if you start feeling better, as this can cause the infection to come back and may lead to antibiotic resistance. Avoid self-adjusting your dose without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction such as hives, rash, itching, swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe diarrhea or diarrhea that is watery or bloody (this could be a serious bowel infection called C. difficile); seizures; signs of kidney problems such as decreased urination or swelling in your legs; yellowing of your skin or eyes; unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of a new infection such as fever or chills that appear while on treatment. Also call your doctor if your infection does not seem to be getting better after a few days.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting cefazolin. However, it is very important that you complete the FULL course of treatment even if you feel better sooner. Stopping too early can allow the bacteria to grow back and make the infection harder to treat. The total length of treatment depends on the type and severity of your infection and is determined by your doctor.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease or reduced kidney function, your doctor may lower your dose or change how often you receive cefazolin to prevent the medicine from building up to harmful levels in your body. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Cefazolin is generally considered safe to use during pregnancy and while breastfeeding, but always inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or nursing. Children: Cefazolin can be used in children, including newborns, but the dose will be carefully calculated based on the child's weight and age. Elderly patients: Older adults may need a lower dose due to reduced kidney function. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Penicillin allergy: If you have had a reaction to penicillin antibiotics in the past, tell your doctor before using cefazolin, as there is a small chance of a cross-reaction.
